newsitem.title: UK: Fresh snow clogs Europe, but temperatures ease.
newsitem.headline: Fresh snow clogs Europe, but temperatures ease.

text.p: Fresh snowfalls blanketed parts of Europe on Sunday, prolonging travel chaos and a deadly freeze, although elsewhere a thaw set in, bringing the threat of flooding as the grip of arctic weather eased.
Southern France was the worst hit, with authorities urging holiday-makers to delay their journey home after bad weather closed several motorways and virtually sealed off ski resorts.
Fresh snow also hit Belgium where six people have perished from cold.
Up to 200 have died across Europe in the worst winter weather for 30 years.
Five froze to death after New Year drinking sessions in Moscow and a record 383 broke bones by slipping on icy pavements, Itar-Tass news agency said.
Temperatures typically sink to minus 20 degrees Celsius (minus 4 Fahrenheit) in the winter in Moscow, where the frost takes an annual toll of people who fall asleep outside and do not wake up.

In Western Europe -- usually far milder than Russia -- the homeless, elderly, and those with too much seasonal spirit inside them have been the main victims of temperatures as low as minus 26 degrees Celsius (minus 15F).
The death toll from the bad weather in Britain rose to 14 with the discovery of a man's body in the snow in the southern English county of Kent. He disappeared following a night out with a friend.

British authorities have turned their attention to flood damage as a thaw raised temperatures across the nation. Fire brigades were called out to help thousands of householders deal with burst pipes and flooded rooms.

An Italian man whose arm and leg were severed trying to board a moving train could have bled to death if snow from the recent cold spell had not stemmed the flow of blood, Italian news agency ANSA said.

Amedeo Barzi, 51, was dragged along by the train for several metres near the northern city of Piacenza on Saturday and spent the whole night outdoors before being discovered by a railway worker at dawn and rushed to hospital.

Hamburg Zoo had to confine its lions to their indoor quarters to prevent them walking over a frozen moat to get out of their compound. A fox in Erfurt Zoo had already used the trick to escape and catch a rare cormorant. Frankfurt airport was forced to cancel over 60 flights because of fresh snowfalls.
In France, several hundred travellers spent Saturday night in schools and town halls after the A20 motorway in the Limousin region was closed.
In the Rhone Valley near Lyon in central France, fresh snow on Sunday seriously disrupted traffic on the A7 Autoroute du Soleil (Sun Motorway).
Further south, three Pyrenees ski resorts were completely sealed off by heavy snowfalls. Three other resorts organised convoys of some 100 vehicles each to allow some skiers to leave.
Rail traffic was also disrupted with thick ice on power cables blocking the Marseille to Paris line and slower diesel trains replacing electric locomotives on the Bordeaux route.

Italy was bracing itself for more snow, cold and high winds on Sunday and Monday, the end of the Christmas holiday, but forecasters did not expect temperatures as low as in recent days, when four died in sub-zero conditions.
Snow fell in Sardinia, which had so far escaped the worst of the bad weather, and in the lagoon city of Venice, the high waters rose another 16 centimetres (six inches).
The northeastern Italian region of Friuli-Venezia-Giulia was gearing up for another cold and windy spell with an exceptionally strong "bora", the chill wind that sweeps along the Adriatic coast.

The cold weather has brought joy to skiers and skaters, with the Netherlands on Saturday able to hold a 200km (125 mile) skating marathon, linking 11 mediaeval cities by canal, for only the 15th time this century.

A 29-year-old sprout farmer won the event, which attracted 16,000 competitors. Race organisers said a 57-year-old competitor had died, probably as a result of a heart attack as he battled against the freezing wind.
